title: Square-zero ring extensions and functorial cotangent extension classes
statement: Let $R\to A$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings and $M$ an $A$-module. Write $L_{A/R}$ for the full standard polynomial cotangent complex [def-trf-cotangent-resolution-data] and $E^1_R(A,M)=\operatorname{Hom}_{D(A)}(L_{A/R},M[1])$, where $M$ is in degree zero and $D(A)$ is the derived category of ordinary modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. An extension is an exact sequence $0\to M\xrightarrow{i}E\xrightarrow{p}A\to0$ of additive groups, where $E$ is a commutative $R$-algebra, $p$ is a surjective $R$-algebra map, $i$ identifies $M$ with the square-zero ideal $\ker(p)$, and the action induced on this ideal is the specified $A$-module action; an extension isomorphism induces the identity on $M$ and $A$. There is a canonical bijection $\mathrm{cl}$ from their isomorphism classes to $E^1_R(A,M)$, sending $A\oplus M$ with multiplication $(a,m)(b,n)=(ab,an+bm)$ to zero. Pushout along an $A$-linear map $M\to M_1$ corresponds to the coefficient map on $E^1$. The Baer sum (fibre product of two extensions over $A$, followed by pushout along addition $M\oplus M\to M$) corresponds to addition on $E^1$. More generally let $f:A\to B$ be an $R$-algebra map, $N$ a $B$-module, and $u:M\to N$ an $A$-linear map. For extensions $E$ of $A$ by $M$ and $F$ of $B$ by $N$, an $R$-algebra map $E\to F$ inducing $f$ and $u$ exists if and only if $u_*\mathrm{cl}(E)=f^*\mathrm{cl}(F)$ in $E^1_R(A,N)$. Here $f^*$ is restriction to $D(A)$ followed by precomposition with the standard cotangent map $L_{A/R}\to L_{B/R}$. These class maps preserve identity maps and composition. No flatness or finiteness hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tags 0GPT (lemma-extensions-of-algebras), 0GPU (remark-extensions-of-algebras), 0GPV (lemma-extensions-of-algebras-functorial), 0GPW (remark-extensions-of-algebras-functorial). Full-complex form follows from cotangent.tex Tag 08RB (lemma-relation-with-naive-cotangent-complex). Baer addition follows from the presentation formula in 0GPU: fibre product pairs the two maps on J/J^2 and coefficient addition adds them.

proof.text: Use the standard polynomial presentation $\alpha:P=R[x_a\mid a\in A]\twoheadrightarrow A$, $x_a\mapsto a$, and put $J=\ker\alpha$, $V=\bigoplus_{a\in A}A\,dx_a$ and $C=[J/J^2\xrightarrow d V]$ in degrees $-1,0$. The universal property of differentials identifies $A\otimes_P\Omega_{P/R}$ with $V$: an assignment to the $dx_a$ extends uniquely by $D(g)=\sum_a\alpha(\partial g/\partial x_a)D(x_a)$, which is a derivation by the product rule on monomials. Thus $d([j])=\sum_a\alpha(\partial j/\partial x_a)dx_a$. The natural truncation comparison gives $\lambda_A:L_{A/R}\to C$ and $\tau_{\ge-1}L_{A/R}\simeq C$. In particular this is a statement about the full standard complex; nothing asserts its lower cohomology vanishes.

Precomposition by $\lambda_A$ gives an additive bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(A)}(C,M[1])\to E^1_R(A,M)$. Indeed the truncation triangle has the form $T\to L_{A/R}\to C\to T[1]$, with $T=\tau_{\le-2}L_{A/R}$ in $D^{\le-2}$. Both $\operatorname{Hom}(T,M[1])$ and $\operatorname{Hom}(T[1],M[1])$ vanish by orthogonality (the target is in $D^{\ge-1}$ and $T[1]\in D^{\le-3}$). Exactness of contravariant Hom on this triangle and its rotation gives surjectivity and injectivity, respectively.

Let $q:C\to(J/J^2)[1]$ be the quotient chain map. The two-term boundary sends $h:J/J^2\to M$ to $h[1]q$ and has kernel the maps $\theta d$ for $\theta:V\to M$. It is surjective: $C$ is the cone of $d$, so $J/J^2\to V\to C\to(J/J^2)[1]$ is a distinguished cone triangle of $D(A)$, whose rotation is the distinguished triangle $V[0]\to C\xrightarrow{\pm q}(J/J^2)[1]\to V[1]$ (the sign does not change the image of precomposition). In it contravariant Hom into $M[1]$ is exact, and $\operatorname{Hom}(V[0],M[1])=\operatorname{Ext}^1_A(V,M)=0$, since $V$ is free, hence projective. The identification $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(A)}(J/J^2,M)=\operatorname{Hom}_A(J/J^2,M)$ is also the Ext-zero clause of the two-term boundary node applied to $[0\to J/J^2]$. Consequently $\kappa_M(h)=h[1]q\lambda_A$ identifies $\operatorname{coker}(\operatorname{Hom}_A(V,M)\xrightarrow{d^*}\operatorname{Hom}_A(J/J^2,M))$ additively with $E^1_R(A,M)$. The stated naturality of the boundary makes this identification commute with coefficients and with maps of presentations.

source.place: Tag 0GPU (remark-extensions-of-algebras), displayed cokernel; derived.tex Tag 0149; algebra.tex Tag 05CF

proof.text: For an extension $E$, choose a lift $y_a\in E$ of every $a\in A$. Polynomial evaluation gives $t:P\to E$ over $R$. Its restriction to $J$ lands in $i(M)$ and annihilates $J^2$, because $i(M)^2=0$; $t(pj)=t(p)i(h([j]))=i(\alpha(p)h([j]))$ proves the resulting $h_t:J/J^2\to M$ is $A$-linear. Set $\mathrm{cl}(E)=\kappa_M(h_t)$. For another lift $t'$, set $D(p)=i^{-1}(t'(p)-t(p))$. Expanding $t'(p)t'(r)$ and using $i(M)^2=0$ gives $D(pr)=\alpha(p)D(r)+\alpha(r)D(p)$; also $D$ is additive and zero on $R$. Thus $D$ corresponds to $\theta:V\to M$ and $h_{t'}-h_t=\theta d$. Step 3 makes the class independent of the choices. An extension isomorphism transports $t$ and leaves $h_t$ unchanged, so this defines a map on isomorphism classes.

source.place: Tag 0GPU (remark-extensions-of-algebras), class formula; Tag 08S5 (lemma-huge-diagram), change of lifts

proof.text: Here is the explicit inverse construction, not an appeal to classification. For an $A$-linear $h:J/J^2\to M$, regard $M$ as a $P$-module via $\alpha$ and form the trivial extension $P\oplus M$. The additive subgroup $I_h=\{(j,-h([j])):j\in J\}$ is an ideal: multiplication by $(p,m)$ sends its displayed element to $(pj,-\alpha(p)h([j]))=(pj,-h([pj]))$, since $\alpha(j)=0$. Set $E_h=(P\oplus M)/I_h$. The map $M\to E_h$, $m\mapsto[(0,m)]$, is injective since $I_h\cap(0\oplus M)=0$. The quotient map $[(p,m)]\mapsto\alpha(p)$ has precisely this image as its kernel: for $p\in J$, $[(p,m)]=[(0,m+h([p]))]$. Its kernel is square-zero with the specified action. The lift $p\mapsto[(p,0)]$ has restriction $h$, so $\mathrm{cl}(E_h)=\kappa_M(h)$. Step 3 therefore proves surjectivity.

source.place: Tag 08S7 (lemma-choices), pushout construction, and Tag 0GPU (remark-extensions-of-algebras); explicit quotient verification

proof.text: For any lift $t:P\to E$, the map $(p,m)\mapsto t(p)+i(m)$ is an $R$-algebra homomorphism $P\oplus M\to E$: its multiplication formula follows from $i(M)^2=0$ and the specified $A$-action. It is surjective since $\alpha$ is surjective. Its kernel is exactly $I_{h_t}$: an element in the kernel first has $p\in J$, then $m=-h_t([p])$. Thus it induces $E_{h_t}\simeq E$ respecting kernel and quotient. If $\mathrm{cl}(E)=\mathrm{cl}(F)$ for two extensions of the same $A$ by $M$, Step 3 gives $h_t-h_s=\theta d$. Replace $s(x_a)$ by $s(x_a)+i_F(\theta(dx_a))$. Polynomial evaluation defines a new lift $s'$; its difference derivation has value $\theta(dx_a)$ on the generators, hence $h_{s'}=h_t$. The two displayed quotient isomorphisms give $E\simeq F$. This proves injectivity. In $A\oplus M$, the lift $p\mapsto(\alpha(p),0)$ restricts to zero, so its class is zero.

For $u:M\to N$ $A$-linear, give $E\oplus N$ multiplication $(e,n)(e',n')=(ee',p(e)n'+p(e')n)$. The antidiagonal subgroup $\{(i(m),-u(m)):m\in M\}$ is an ideal, as multiplication by $(e,n)$ sends its element to $(i(p(e)m),-u(p(e)m))$. Its quotient $E^u$ maps onto $A$ with kernel $N$ embedded by $n\mapsto[(0,n)]$: intersection with $0\oplus N$ is zero, and $[(i(m),n)]=[(0,n+u(m))]$. This is the coefficient pushout, since a compatible map into any other extension is forced to send $[(e,n)]$ to the sum of the images of $e$ and $n$, and that formula is multiplicative. The lift $p_0\mapsto[(t(p_0),0)]$ has conormal map $u h_t$. Thus $\mathrm{cl}(E^u)=u_*\mathrm{cl}(E)$ by the naturality of the boundary.

source.place: Tag 0GPW (remark-extensions-of-algebras-functorial), coefficient pushout; Tag 0GPU, formula for its class

proof.text: For the fibre product $E_1\times_A E_2$, its kernel is $M\oplus M$ and paired polynomial lifts give conormal map $(h_1,h_2)$. Pushing out by $(m_1,m_2)\mapsto m_1+m_2$ gives conormal map $h_1+h_2$. Since the two-term boundary is additive, the resulting class is $\kappa_M(h_1+h_2)=\kappa_M(h_1)+\kappa_M(h_2)$. This is exactly the asserted Baer-sum compatibility.

source.place: Tag 0GPU (remark-extensions-of-algebras), presentation formula, applied to paired lifts and addition

proof.text: Let $f:A\to B$ and let $F$ be an extension of $B$ by $N$. Put $P_B=R[x_b\mid b\in B]$ with kernel $K$ and let $\varphi:P\to P_B$ send $x_a$ to $x_{f(a)}$. If $s:P_B\to F$ is a polynomial lift, the ring fibre product $F_f=A\times_B F$ is an extension of $A$ by $N$, with lift $p_0\mapsto(\alpha(p_0),s\varphi(p_0))$. Its conormal map is $h_s\bar\varphi:J/J^2\to N$, where $\bar\varphi([j])=[\varphi(j)]\in K/K^2$. The naturality of the comparison $L\to C$ identifies the chain map induced by $\varphi$ with the standard cotangent map after restricting coefficients to $A$. The boundary commutes with this chain map, so $\mathrm{cl}(F_f)=\kappa_N(h_s\bar\varphi)=f^*\mathrm{cl}(F)$. No derived tensor base-change is used: this is restriction of the target complex followed by precomposition, precisely as in the statement.

source.place: Tag 0GPW (remark-extensions-of-algebras-functorial), final presentation diagram; cotangent.tex Tag 08RB

proof.text:
An $R$-algebra map $H:E\to F$ inducing $f,u$ defines a map of extensions of $A$ by $N$,
$E^u\to F_f$, $[(e,n)]\mapsto(p(e),H(e)+i_F(n))$. It kills the antidiagonal relations; multiplication follows from the square-zero product and the specified module action. It induces the identity on $A$ and $N$, and hence is bijective: a kernel element lies in $N$ and is zero; for surjectivity lift the quotient coordinate and then correct the difference by an element of $N$. Conversely an isomorphism $E^u\simeq F_f$ composed with $E\to E^u$ and $F_f\to F$ gives the required $H$. By injectivity of the classification already proved, such an isomorphism exists exactly when $\mathrm{cl}(E^u)=\mathrm{cl}(F_f)$. Steps 7 and 9 identify this with $u_*\mathrm{cl}(E)=f^*\mathrm{cl}(F)$.

Finally the class maps preserve identity and composition. On standard polynomial presentations the maps $x_a\mapsto x_{f(a)}$ have these properties strictly, as do the standard cotangent maps. The comparison and boundary are natural. Thus for $A\xrightarrow f B\xrightarrow g C$ restriction and precomposition give $(gf)^*=f^*g^*$, and for coefficient maps $M\xrightarrow u N\xrightarrow v N'$ postcomposition gives $(vu)_*=v_*u_*$. Precomposition and postcomposition commute by associativity, and both send identities to identities. All the constructions used arbitrary sets of generators and arbitrary modules, so impose no finiteness or flatness condition.
